chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

A man from Hudhayl used to insult the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. News of that reached the Prophet, so he said, “Who will deal with this man?” Two men from the Anṣār stood and said, “We will, O Messenger of Allah.” They set out until they came to ʿUranah and asked about him. Then there he was, receiving his sheep, so they caught up with him between his family and his sheep. They did not give salām to him. He said, “Who are you two, and what are your names?” They said to him, “Are you so-and-so son of so-and-so?” He said, “Yes.” Then they dismounted and struck his neck.

Muḥammad ibn Muslim said: I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, “What do you think—if a man now were to insult the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, would he be killed?” He said, “If you do not fear for yourself, then kill him.”

key_terms.إِنْ لَمْ تَخَفْ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ: if you do not fear for your own safety
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.سَبَّ النَّبِيَّ: insulted the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.فَضَرَبَا عُنُقَهُ: they struck his neck, meaning they killed him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on someone who insults the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident involving a man who insulted the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and then records Imam Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام giving a ruling regarding one who insults the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. The report is significant in the chapter on false accusation, insult, allusion, explicit abuse, and false testimony, and it presents a legal ruling tied to the condition of personal safety.
